title: Flophouse: Life on the Bowery

description.main: Portraits and testimony from residents of four Bowery flophouses, text by David Isay and Stacy Abramson, photographs by Harvey Wang.
description.extended:
Portraits and spoken testimony from the men who lived in four of the Bowery's remaining flophouses, with text by David Isay and Stacy Abramson and photographs by Harvey Wang.

A short history of the Bowery opens the book. The rest is divided into four sections, one for each hotel: the White House, the Providence, the Andrews and the Sunshine. Each photograph is paired with a page of text in which the resident describes his own life. The book grew out of an NPR All Things Considered program narrated by Nate Smith, manager of the Sunshine Hotel.

Isay is executive producer of Sound Portraits Productions, where Abramson is a producer. Wang is a New York photographer whose earlier books include Harvey Wang's New York (W.W. Norton, 1990) and Holding On (W.W. Norton, 1995).
